Subject: Private runtime dark-launch — DNS & cert questions

Hi Aditya,

Thanks again for the walkthrough today. A couple of quick asks from our infra team as we prepare the dark-launch window for the private runtime in our VPC:

1) We want a list of recommended DNS surface patterns (ephemeral subdomains vs. stable private FQDNs) and how Redwood expects to validate ownership for each.
2) For the dark-launch traffic, can Redwood present a different TLS identity (cert) than production while still keeping mTLS validation on our side?
3) We need a short failure/fallback matrix — if cert issuance for the ephemeral names stalls, what are the safe rollback options?

We plan to run the dark-launch in the US-east-1 VPC from Oct 19–23. Can you share a brief runbook and any artifacts the Oricon infra team should prep (CSRs, DNS delegation, expected TTLs)?

Sofia

Sofia —

Thanks for the clear list. Looping in Marissa (solutions), Neha (security), Jonas (infra) and Mina (SRE) so we can put a concise ops playbook together. High-level answers first, full runbook attached.

High-level:
- DNS patterns: we recommend ephemeral subdomains for dark-launch (e.g., dl-<env>.orion.internal.redwood) with a short TTL (60s) and CNAME pointing to our internal gateway. Stable private FQDNs should be used only when you want a long-lived service identity and for production cutover.
- Ownership proof: For ephemeral names, a signed CSR + DNS TXT proof (token) is sufficient. For stable FQDNs we prefer a delegated NS or a pre-provisioned certificate uploaded to your KMS/HSM and an assertion via signed metadata.
- TLS identity during dark-launch: Yes — we can present a distinct cert chain for the dark cluster. We support presenting an alternate SAN set and a separate CA chain for test tiers. This preserves mTLS on your client side as long as your trust anchors include the dark-launch CA.
- Failure/fallback options: see attached matrix. Short summary: (1) If ephemeral cert issuance fails, fail closed to the test gateway and route production traffic to the existing prod gateway; (2) If DNS propagation delays occur, use a static CNAME fallback to a stable host; (3) If CA chain trust fails, use a pre-shared (uploaded) cert as emergency override.

Action items for Orion infra (what we need from you):
- CSR or DNS TXT token for each ephemeral subdomain (format in attached runbook)
- Pre-approved emergency cert to upload to your account (PEM) (optional but recommended)
- Confirmation of the short TTL policy and whether you can create the CNAMEs from your resolver zone

I attached: dark-launch-matrix.xlsx (decision matrix) and private-runtime-ddt.pdf (deployment & diagnostics checklist).

I'll follow up with a one-page ops checklist for the engineer executing the window.

—Aditya

Adding a few engineering details that are important for the runbook:

1) TLS key rotation window — for dark-launch we recommend a rotation period aligned with the window end (rotate keys on cutover to avoid stale trust).
2) OCSP/CRL considerations — for ephemeral certs, we prefer short-lived certs (24–48 hours) to avoid CRL/OCSP lookup overhead; Redwood will also support stapling at the gateway.
3) DNS resolvers — if Orion runs split-horizon resolvers, ensure the test subdomain resolves to our test gateway IPs from the client VPC route table; otherwise create an explicit VPC resolver rule.

I also exported a simple TTL vs. rollback-latency table into the matrix (see worksheet 2). Minor wording change in step 4 of the checklist around pre-seeding the cache.

Marissa

Sofia —

Couple of security notes from our side before your dark-launch:

- Trust anchors: for the dark CA we will publish a separate CA bundle. Please tell us if Orion's HSM/KMS policy requires hardware-backed validation before adding that CA to your trust store. If so, we can provide an alternate approach (pre-signed cert upload) and a short audit artifact for compliance.
- Audit and retention: Redwood will emit token-level audit events for every certificate bind/issue during the window. If Orion needs extended retention for these logs, indicate the retention window (we can arrange a 90/180/365 day export).
- Network segmentation: ensure that the test gateway lives in a segregated subnet with security group limiting ingress only to the Oricon test IP ranges. We'll share a small iptables-friendly CIDR list for the runbook.

Final ask: please confirm whether you want the dark-launch CA to be automatically removed from your trust chain at the end of the window (default: yes) or retained for a longer evaluation period. If you opt to retain, we will create a monthly rotation schedule and provide the CSR rotation artifacts.

If you confirm today, we'll finalize the runbook and a one-click checklist for your infra engineer.

Thanks —
